The invoice tracking dashboard and finance dashboard generators both start from this shape. ⚙️ The Automation Ladder That Pays for Itself Trigger Timing Action Owner after Logged as Due date approaching 7 days before Courtesy email with invoice and pay link Finance Touch: courtesy Terms lapsed Day 1 past due Reminder with balance and pay link Finance Touch: reminder 1 Still open Day 14 Second reminder, slightly firmer Finance Touch: reminder 2 Still open Day 30 Create AM call task with client history attached Account manager Task + touch Promise date missed Same day Notify AM and reopen the call task Account manager Touch: broken promise Crosses 60 days On bucket change Add to principal review list Principal Escalation Payment recorded On field update Recalculate balance, close reminders, notify AM — Touch: paid Two rules keep automations from becoming noise. First, every automated touch must write to the invoice record , or two people will nag the same client on the same afternoon. Second, turn on exactly one automation at a time and let it run a full week before adding the next. Reference guides: automation triggers for what starts a run, automation actions for what it does, and schedule for the time-based checks aging depends on. Adjacent generators once the ladder works: monthly billing statement generator , estimate to invoice converter , and cash flow management workflow . 🏗️ What the Board Owns vs What You Pair Honest boundaries beat feature checklists. Job Owned AR board handles it Pair with Bucket views, owners, chase history Yes, this is the core — Reminder and escalation sequences Yes — Delivery context on the invoice row Yes, linked projects — Client-visible invoice status Yes, scoped app views — Payment processing No Your existing processor Tax filing, payroll, reconciliation No QuickBooks, Xero, your CPA Full double-entry general ledger No Accounting suite Complex interest and late-fee accrual Partially, via fields you define Accounting suite for anything the ledger must reflect High-volume per-invoice dunning at scale No Dedicated collections service If anyone — including us — tells you an owned board replaces your general ledger, that is overselling. It replaces the Monday export and the shadow spreadsheet, which is a much better trade than it sounds. 📋 Migration Checklist: Spreadsheet or Aging Report to an Owned Board Run two weeks in parallel. Do not cut over during a payroll crunch. Week 0: Decide the nouns Name the four you cannot lose: client, invoice, balance, due date Name the optional ones: retainer month, SOW number, milestone, AP contact, promise date Write down what stays where it is: accounting suite, payroll, payment processor Write the collections policy before you chase anything (pause rules, plan authority, write-off threshold) Week 1: Generate and load truth Generate the accounts receivable aging dashboard Export open invoices from your accounting suite and import real rows, not demo data Reconcile the imported total against the ledger aging report to the dollar Link each invoice to its active project or retainer month Assign an owner to every open row — no orphans Invite the finance lead first, then account managers Week 2: Automations, portal, review Turn on one automation: the day-1 reminder Add the collections workflow for the 30 and 60-day steps Add a scoped client status view only for clients who ask about invoices Add an AR agent after the board holds real history, not before Freeze the old spreadsheet for new rows; keep it read-only Cutover rules New invoices land on the board the day they are issued. The accounting suite stays authoritative for the ledger; the board is authoritative for status and next action. One system owns each noun. The board owns bucket and owner. The ledger owns recognized revenue. Day Focus Done looks like 1 Generate the board Columns match how your team talks 2 Import open invoices Board total ties to the ledger aging report 3 Link projects and retainer months Two clients show delivered work on the row 4 Assign owners Zero open invoices without a name 5 One automation live Day-1 reminders send and log a touch 6-7 AM feedback Rename one confusing field 8-10 30 and 60-day steps A real call task fires with context attached 11-12 Client status view One client checks status without emailing finance 13-14 Parallel quiet Old spreadsheet has zero new rows 🆚 Side-by-Side: Choosing an AR Aging Tracker Question QuickBooks Harvest / FreshBooks Spreadsheet Taskade Genesis Product shape Accounting suite Time-to-invoice tool A file you maintain Living ops app platform Aging view Report you re-run Invoice status list Formula column Live bucket views Chase workflow Not modeled Light reminders Manual Owners, tasks, escalation Delivery context Absent Hours only Whatever you paste Linked projects and milestones Client-visible status Rarely Invoice links No Scoped app view per client Who reshapes fields Accountant or vendor Vendor Anyone, dangerously You, with Taskade EVE Best for Books and filing Hours-driven billing Under ten invoices Owning the chase Capability depth vs ownership Capability Accounting suite Owned AR board Aging arithmetic Excellent Excellent when modeled General ledger and tax Excellent Not a strength; pair it Chase task assignment Weak First-class Automated dunning cadence Add-on or manual Built from triggers Partial-payment balance tracking Excellent Strong when you model balance Custom fields for your billing model Constrained Change the app yourself Roll-up across many clients Report-driven Views across the workspace AI grounded on your invoices Vendor features Agents on your Projects 🕗 A Day in the Life on an Owned AR Board 08:10 Finance opens the board. Three invoices crossed into 31-60 overnight. Each already has an owner and an auto-created call task. Nobody hunted through an export. 09:30 An account manager opens one of those tasks. The client's payment history, last delivered milestone, and previous promise date are on the row. The call takes four minutes instead of twenty. 11:00 A client pays two of three open invoices. The balance field updates, the invoice drops to a partial row rather than vanishing, and queued reminders for the paid rows close themselves. 13:45 A retainer client hits 62 days. The board adds them to the principal's review list automatically. No Slack thread required. 15:20 The principal opens the review list. Five rows, one decision each: call, pause, plan, or write off. Every decision gets logged on the invoice, so next month's conversation starts from record rather than memory. 16:40 An AR agent drafts next week's escalation notes from the touch log. A human edits two of them and sends. The board is the same one the whole team used all day. That day requires no general ledger inside Taskade, and no exports. It requires a board people trust and a policy written before the pressure arrived. 📈 Forecasting Cash From Buckets, Honestly A raw open-AR total overstates next month's cash. Weight each bucket by how much of it historically lands. Bucket Open balance Collection weight Forecast contribution Current $46,000 0.95 $43,700 1-30 $22,000 0.90 $19,800 31-60 $9,500 0.70 $6,650 61-90 $4,200 0.45 $1,890 90+ $3,300 0.20 $660 Total $85,000 — $72,700 That $12,300 gap between headline AR and weighted forecast is the number that should drive a hiring or spending decision — not the $85,000. Derive your own weights from twelve months of actual collection outcomes, then revisit them quarterly. Pair the board with a financial reporting workflow or the revenue ops board when leadership wants trend lines rather than a snapshot. Two leading indicators earn a place on the leadership view: the 60-plus total, and its two-week direction. A rising 60-plus total for two consecutive weeks is a hiring-freeze signal well before the bank balance says so. 🗣 Dunning Tone Guide Consistent tone protects relationships while cash comes in. Automations handle timing; humans choose words on escalation rows. Age Tone Channel Who sends 7 days before due Helpful, transactional Automated email Automation 1-14 days late Friendly, assumes oversight Automated email Automation 30 days late Direct, references delivered work Phone call Account manager 60 days late Firm, presents pause options Scheduled call Principal 90+ days late Formal, states next step plainly Written, then call Principal Sample 60-plus escalation note: Acme Co, $12,400 open across two invoices. AM spoke on the 12th, client promised payment by the 20th, nothing received. Recommendation: pause March deliverables until 50% clears, offer a two-part plan, notify the principal. Logged on invoice rows 1042 and 1047. Notes like that turn AR from vague anxiety into a decision with a paper trail. Staff should never have to invent collections policy under stress — document pause rules, payment-plan authority, and write-off thresholds once, then link the policy inside your agency back office portal so new finance hires inherit it. 🚫 Five Mistakes That Break AR Boards Mistake Why it hurts Fix Charts instead of actions Dashboards do not call clients Every row carries an owner and a next action Tracking original amount only Partial payments make buckets lie Track remaining balance as the primary field One portal for every client Leaks other clients' data Scope visibility per app user Untracked touches Two people nag the same client the same day Automations write to the invoice record Two systems claiming the same noun Reconciliation becomes a weekly chore Board owns status; ledger owns recognized revenue 👥 Finance and Account Manager Handoffs Finance owns buckets and escalation. Account managers own relationship context. The board should encode that split rather than rely on goodwill: assign the account manager at 30 days, the principal at 60, and keep finance as the standing owner of everything younger. Meeting notes on the client record prevent the "I already talked to them" surprise that makes an agency look disorganized to the one person holding a check. Pair the AR board with an agency client CRM when the relationship history matters as much as the balance, and with a retainer hours burn tracker when over-servicing is the actual reason invoices get disputed. Retainers and fixed-fee projects both belong on one board, but the row must say which it is. Pausing a retainer skips a monthly cycle. Pausing project work may breach an SOW. Collectors need to see the difference before they threaten anything — link project invoices to milestones and retainer invoices to month labels via the agency retainer scope tracker . 🔐 Client-Visible Status Without Leaking Anything Some agencies expose invoice status to clients so finance questions stop landing in delivery channels. Scoped app users make that safe — each client sees their own rows and nothing else. Custom domains are available on Business and above if you want the status view to live on your own URL. Start from the agency client portal or the accounting client portal , and read self-updating client portals for the maintenance pattern. Browse the Community Gallery to see how other teams shaped finance-facing views before you build yours. ❓ FAQ: AR Aging Trackers for Agencies What is the best AR aging tracker for agencies in 2026? Taskade Genesis for an owned ops board where collectors actually work — buckets, owners, chase history, and automations tied to delivery context. QuickBooks for authoritative books and filing. Harvest for shops where AR starts from tracked hours. Generate the AR aging dashboard and validate it against your ledger before you change anything else. Can Taskade Genesis replace QuickBooks? No, and it should not try. The board owns operational aging, chase workflow, client-visible status, and escalation. QuickBooks keeps tax filing, payroll integration, reconciliation, and accountant handoff. Most agencies run both and make one system authoritative per noun. Can I import open invoices from QuickBooks? Yes. Export the open-invoice list as CSV, map columns into the board, and reconcile the total against the aging report to the dollar before you enable any automation. A board that disagrees with the ledger on day one will never be trusted. How do I handle partial payments? Model balance as the field the bucket derives from, and keep amount as history. A 60-day invoice that is 70% paid is a different collections problem than a full-value one, and treating them the same is how agencies chase the wrong client. Does Taskade Genesis calculate interest on late invoices? You can define fields and derived values for your own late-fee policy. Anything the general ledger must reflect for tax or audit purposes should still be computed in your accounting suite so the two never disagree. How many automations should I start with? One. Turn on the day-1 reminder, let it run a full week, confirm every send wrote a touch to the invoice record, then add the 30-day account manager task. Shipping seven automations on day one guarantees a client gets nagged three times before lunch. Can clients see their invoice status without a workspace seat? Yes. Scoped app users show each client their own rows only. Never give a client a workspace seat to check an invoice — pair the AR board with a client portal and read app users for the setup. How is this different from a BI dashboard? BI charts summarize exported data. An AR ops board is where collectors work: sort buckets, log calls, snooze reminders, escalate. If nobody can take an action from a screen, it is a report, not a board. See ops dashboard builders for the broader category. Do we need an AI agent for this? Not on day one. An agent on empty sample rows is theater. Once the board holds real payment history, an agent can draft call scripts, summarize a client's pattern, and flag chronic late payers. Add it in week three, not week one. What is the fastest way to start? Open the accounts receivable aging dashboard generator, import your open invoices from CSV, assign an owner to every row, then enable the day-1 reminder before Monday's leadership review. 📚 Related Reading Ops dashboard builders — the wider agency ops board category AI invoice automation — the billing side of the same loop AI invoice generators — where invoices come from before they age Agency retainer tracker — scope and burn beside the balance Best agency management software — full-stack agency tooling AI for agencies — broader agency automation patterns Automate accounting and bookkeeping — what belongs in the ledger AI finance workspaces for founders — leadership-level views Build a finance dashboard — hands-on walkthrough Multi-client agency ops hub — delivery plus billing spine Client billing workflow — upstream of aging Agency capacity board — why invoices slip in the first place Taskade Community Gallery — live apps you can clone 🚀 Own the Board, Keep the Ledger AR aging is operations, not accounting cosplay. The board exists so someone calls the client before payroll panic — and so the person who calls already knows what shipped, what was promised, and who promised it. Keep your accounting suite authoritative for books, tax, and payroll. Move the chase onto a board your team owns, where buckets update themselves, owners are named, and every touch is written down. That is the whole trade: ▲ Memory holds the invoices and the history, ■ Intelligence proposes the next move, ● Execution sends it and logs the outcome. title: UNIFI®, Makers of REPREVE®, Reports Fourth Quarter Revenue Growth, Higher Margins, and Cash Generation
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about UNIFI, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Fourth quarter revenue growth, disciplined cost execution, and stronger cash generation highlight continued progress in operational turnaround GREENSBORO, N.C.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 19, 2026-- Unifi, Inc. (NYSE: UFI), the makers of REPREVE® and one of the world’s leading innovators in recycled and synthetic yarns, today released operating results for the fourth fiscal quarter and fiscal year ended June 28, 2026. Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2026 Highlights Net sales were $144.2 million, an increase of 4.1% from the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. Revenues from REPREVE Fiber products were $40.2 million and represented 28% of net sales. Gross profit was $14.3 million and gross margin was 9.9%, compared to gross loss of $1.1 million and gross margin of (0.8)% for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. SG&A expenses were $11.8 million, a decrease of 1.0% from the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, primarily driven by cost reduction efforts. Net loss was $1.2 million, or $0.06 per share, compared to net income of $15.5 million, or $0.82 per share, for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, which included a $35.8 million gain on the sale of a manufacturing facility, partially offset by $10.6 million in transition costs. Adjusted EBITDA* was $8.2 million, compared to $(4.1) million for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. Cash provided by operating activities was $2.1 million during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and $26.5 million during fiscal 2026. Debt principal was $92.4 million and Net Debt* was $67.4 million at June 28, 2026. Following the fourth fiscal quarter, the Company entered into an agreement to sell certain non-strategic real estate assets within the Americas Segment for $60.0 million of gross proceeds. Upon closing, the transaction will significantly enhance financial flexibility, support debt reduction, and further strengthen the balance sheet, with no expected impact on customer service or daily operations. Eddie Ingle, Chief Executive Officer of Unifi, Inc., stated, “We closed fiscal 2026 with clear momentum, highlighted by meaningful improvement in profitability and cash generation. These results reflect disciplined execution of our cost reduction, operational optimization, and portfolio management initiatives, each of which have driven lower our revenue break-even point. As we enter fiscal 2027, UNIFI is operating from a healthier financial position, with a more focused cost structure and a balance sheet that we expect to further strengthen through the planned sale of non-strategic real estate assets.” Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2026 Compared to Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2025 Net sales increased to $144.2 million from $138.5 million, primarily due to higher sales from the Brazil Segment, partially offset by tepid customer ordering patterns in the Americas and Asia Segments stemming from geopolitical, trade, and tariff-related uncertainty. Gross profit increased to $14.3 million from $(1.1) million. Americas Segment gross profit increased by $8.6 million, primarily as a result of multi-year cost reduction efforts. Brazil Segment gross profit increased by $6.4 million, primarily due to favorable pricing dynamics. Asia Segment gross profit increased by $0.5 million, primarily due to an improved sales mix. Operating income was $2.4 million, compared to $15.1 million in the prior period, primarily reflecting the absence of the gain from the sale of a manufacturing facility recognized in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, which was partially offset by transition costs. Net loss was $1.2 million compared to net income of $15.5 million, which included a gain in fiscal 2025. Adjusted EBITDA* was $8.2 million, a significant increase versus $(4.1) million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 Compared to Fiscal 2025 Gross margin improved 420 basis points, from 1.5% to 5.7%. SG&A expenses decreased $4.3 million, from $49.0 million to $44.7 million. Debt principal declined $15.6 million, from $108.0 million to $92.4 million. Cash provided by operating activities increased $47.8 million, from $(21.3) million to $26.5 million. Capital expenditures decreased $5.5 million, from $10.5 million to $5.0 million. Fiscal 2027 and First Quarter Outlook During fiscal 2027, the Company expects: To focus on leveraging its improved cost footprint while investing in innovation. Managing the balance sheet to ensure that the Company remains better positioned to capitalize on improved business conditions and grow over time. Sales and profitability to improve from fiscal 2026 as the Company realizes full-year benefits from portfolio management actions, cost containment initiatives, and improved operating execution. During the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the Company expects year-over-year segment results as follows: Brazil Segment sales and profitability to improve as the Company leverages its competitive position and advantageous supply chain dynamics. The Asia Segment will remain pressured due to regional softness and geopolitical volatility. Cost savings and stable demand will increase profitability in the Americas Segment with continued growth in margin accretive revenues from value-added products and Beyond Apparel initiatives. Ingle concluded, “As we enter fiscal 2027, we are seeing encouraging signs across several areas of our business, including Beyond Apparel, which continues to contribute to our improving financial performance. We remain focused on positioning the business for long-term growth, driving disciplined capital allocation, and executing additional initiatives designed to further strengthen our businesses. While UNIFI has entered the new fiscal year in a position of greater financial strength, our focus remains on executing our strategy, serving our customers, and building on the momentum that we have established that will help create long-term value for our shareholders.” * Adjusted Net Income (Loss), Adjusted EBITDA, and Net Debt are non-GAAP financial measures. The schedules included in this press release reconcile each non-GAAP financial measure to its most directly comparable GAAP financial measure. Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2026 Earnings Conference Call UNIFI will provide additional commentary regarding its fourth quarter and fiscal 2026 results and other developments during its earnings conference call on August 20, 2026, at 8:30 a.m., Eastern Time. The call can be accessed via a live audio webcast on UNIFI’s website at http://investor.unifi.com . Additional supporting materials and information related to the call will also be available on UNIFI’s website. About UNIFI UNIFI, Inc. (NYSE: UFI) is a global leader in fiber science and sustainable synthetic textiles. Using proprietary recycling technology, UNIFI is a pioneer in scaling the transformation of post-industrial and post-consumer waste into sustainable products. Through REPREVE, the world’s leading brand of traceable, recycled fiber and resin, UNIFI is changing the way industries think about the materials they use – and reuse. A vertically-integrated manufacturer, the company has direct operations in the United States, Colombia, El Salvador, and Brazil, and sales offices all over the world. UNIFI envisions a future where circular and sustainable solutions are the only choice. For more information about UNIFI, visit www.unifi.com . About REPREVE® Made by UNIFI, Inc. (NYSE: UFI), REPREVE® is the global leader in recycled performance fibers and resins. Using proprietary recycling technology, REPREVE leverages multiple waste sources, including single-use plastic bottles, ocean-bound plastic, textile waste, and recycled yarn. REPREVE has transformed more than 46 billion plastic bottles and 1 billion T-shirts’ worth of textile waste into recycled fiber, powering globally scalable products for world-leading brands. Made traceable with FiberPrint® technology and certified by U-TRUST®, REPREVE spans apparel, footwear, furnishings, industrial, medical, military, mobility, and packaging. For more information about REPREVE, visit www.repreve.com . title: 16th Annual Avista Charity Golf Tournament raises $16,000 benefitting Montana animal shelter
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Avista Corporation 's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: << Back PDF Version THOMPSON FALLS, Mont. – Aug. 18, 2026: Avista Utilities is proud to announce that its 16th Annual Charity Golf Scramble and Silent Auction, held on August 15, 2026, at River’s Bend Golf Course in Thompson Falls, raised $16,461 in support of the Thompson River Animal Care Shelter (TRACS). For the last twenty years, this Montana nonprofit has rescued thousands of animals in need of medical care and shelter to provide a second chance at a loving home. "The generosity of the Avista team and every golfer, sponsor, volunteer and donor will help us provide lifesaving care and find loving homes for more animals in Sanders County and many other areas around the country. Your support will allow us to continue our mission of protecting and caring for the most vulnerable pets. We're deeply thankful for the donations raised and the community that made it possible,” said Wanda Thorpe, founder of TRACS. Avista has had a presence in Northwest Montana since 1959, when the Noxon Rapids Dam began generating hydropower and contributing to the region through job creation and long-term local investment. Its presence in Montana has brought lasting benefits, including support for environmental resources and community development. Today, Avista manages stewardship along the Clark Fork River and 28 public recreation sites, offers scholarships to local students, and supports other philanthropic initiatives. “Community partnerships are at the heart of what we do at Avista. By working together to support meaningful causes, we can make a greater impact and help build stronger, more vibrant communities," said Sean Kelly, Avista Noxon Rapids Dam chief operator and golf tournament committee chair. Each year, Avista chooses a local 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization to benefit from the charity golf tournament and co-host the event. Organizations are selected with an emphasis on those that serve a vulnerable population and strengthen the local community. More information can be found at myavista.com/Montana . Since the tournament started in 2009, the event has raised over $244,666 for local causes. Media package with photos and captions is available here for download. Please courtesy Avista Utilities when using this content. Avista Corp. is an energy company involved in the production, transmission and distribution of energy as well as other energy-related businesses. Avista Utilities is our operating division that provides electric service to 429,000 customers and natural gas to 386,000 customers. Our service territory covers 34,000 square miles in eastern Washington, northern Idaho and parts of southern and eastern Oregon, with a population of 1.5 million. AERC is an Avista subsidiary that, through its subsidiary AEL&P, provides retail electric service to 18,000 customers in the city and borough of Juneau, Alaska. Our stock is traded under the ticker symbol “AVA”. title: Sagimet Biosciences Receives FDA “Study May Proceed” Letter and IND Clearance for Phase 3 Trial in Acne in Adolescent and Adult Patients
summary: Phase 3 clinical trial of denifanstat in moderate to severe acne patients in the U.S. on track to initiate in second half of 2026 FOSTER CITY, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sagimet Biosciences Inc. (Nasdaq: SGMT), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics
body_text: Phase 3 clinical trial of denifanstat in moderate to severe acne patients in the U.S. on track to initiate in second half of 2026 FOSTER CITY, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sagimet Biosciences Inc. (Nasdaq: SGMT), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics targeting dysfunctional metabolic and fibrotic pathways, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the Investigational New Drug (IND) application and issued a “Study May Proceed” letter for the company’s Phase 3 clinical trial of fatty acid synthase (FASN) inhibitor denifanstat in moderate to severe acne. The Phase 3 clinical trial is on track to initiate in the second half of 2026. “This letter marks an important regulatory milestone for denifanstat,” said Andreas Grauer, MD, Chief Medical Officer of Sagimet. “The Phase 3 clinical trial is intended to enroll approximately 800 US patients, with 450 expected to be adolescents, using well-accepted co-primary endpoints that will be assessed at the end of the 12-week randomized double-blind period, followed by a 40-week open-label extension to evaluate long-term safety. We appreciate the FDA's review and look forward to advancing into Phase 3 this year.” “Clearance of the IND and receipt of the “Study May Proceed” letter is a decisive step in our clinical development of denifanstat for acne,” said David Happel, Chief Executive Officer of Sagimet. “We are on track to initiate the trial and start dosing patients this year. As an oral once-daily FASN inhibitor, denifanstat offers a novel mechanism of action to treat acne, and we look forward to offering this novel treatment option, if approved, to a currently underserved patient population.” About the Phase 3 Clinical Trial The multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 clinical trial of denifanstat in moderate to severe acne is intended to enroll approximately 800 U.S. patients aged 12 years and older, of which 450 are expected to be adolescents aged 12 to 17 years. Patients will be randomized 2:1 to receive denifanstat 50 mg or placebo once daily for 12 weeks. The trial has three co-primary endpoints assessed at week 12: the proportion of patients achieving treatment success in a global assessment score, defined as at least a 2-point reduction from baseline with a score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear); absolute change in inflammatory skin lesion counts from baseline; and absolute change in non-inflammatory skin lesion counts from baseline. Patients completing the double-blind period will be eligible to enter a 40-week open-label extension evaluating the long-term safety of denifanstat. About Denifanstat Denifanstat is an oral, once-daily FASN inhibitor in development for the treatment of moderate to severe acne. In trials conducted by our license partner, Ascletis BioScience Co. Ltd. (Ascletis) in China, Denifanstat met all primary and secondary endpoints in a 12 week randomized, double-blind Phase 3 clinical trial in moderate to severe acne vulgaris and was generally well-tolerated and showed improvements in all efficacy endpoints measured at 52 weeks (secondary endpoints of the trial) in an open-label Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating its long-term safety in patients with moderate to severe acne. Denifanstat is being developed by Ascletis as ASC40 for acne in China and by Sagimet in the rest of world. About Acne Acne is one of the most common skin conditions in the U.S., with approximately 50 million Americans affected annually and more than 5 million seeking medical treatment for acne each year. Acne affects around 85% of persons between the ages of 12 and 24. Moderate to severe acne accounts for 20% of acne sufferers, or approximately 10 million people in the U.S. annually. There is no cure for acne, and due to its pathology, most patients require chronic management and multiple annual courses of treatment for flare control. About Sagimet Biosciences Sagimet is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel FASN inhibitors designed to target dysfunctional metabolic and fibrotic pathways in conditions resulting from the overproduction of the fatty acid, palmitate. FASN is a regulator of lipid synthesis, and a key pathway implicated in multiple diseases, such as acne, MASH and certain FASN-dependent tumor types. title: Liberty Global Completes Buyout of VodafoneZiggo
summary: Liberty Global completes its acquisition of Vodafone's 50% shareholding in VodafoneZiggo, paving the way for the creation of Ziggo Group
body_text: Liberty Global today announced the completion of its acquisition of Vodafone Group Plc’s 50% shareholding in VodafoneZiggo , paving the way for the creation of Ziggo Group, the Benelux connectivity champion with 13 million customers and €6.6bn of revenue*. As part of the transaction, Vodafone has received approximately €1.0 billion in cash and a 10% equity interest in Ziggo Group, which will hold Liberty Global’s interests in VodafoneZiggo in the Netherlands and Telenet in Belgium and Luxembourg. Liberty Global holds the remaining 90% of Ziggo Group. The completion of the transaction marks a significant milestone in Liberty Global’s strategy to unlock value in its telecommunications portfolio. As previously announced, the company plans to list Ziggo Group in Amsterdam in 2027 by spinning off the 90% held by Liberty Global to its shareholders. The proposed spin-off is intended to be tax free for US shareholders of Liberty Global (with evaluation of tax treatment in other jurisdictions ongoing), and follows the successful spin-off of the company’s Swiss telecoms group, Sunrise, which has delivered significant returns for shareholders. Plans for the listing of Ziggo Group are already under way with VodafoneZiggo CEO Stephen van Rooyen appointed CEO of Ziggo Group and Sunrise CFO Jany Fruytier becoming CFO once Ziggo Group begins operations in September. The financial separation of Telenet’s and Wyre’s credit facilities has also been completed following the Belgian Competition Authority’s approval of the network collaboration in Flanders between Wyre and Proximus. Wyre has drawn €2.71bn ($3.13bn) of debt from its €4.35bn ($5.02bn) bank facility. The use of proceeds included a €398m ($460m) dividend to Telenet and the repayment of a €1.98bn ($2.28bn) intercompany loan to Telenet. Telenet then used proceeds to repay €2.12bn ($2.45bn) of its own debt, maturing in 2028. In addition, €1.2-1.4bn ($1.4-1.6bn) of asset disposals across the Ziggo Group (50% of Telenet’s stake in Wyre, VodafoneZiggo’s tower portfolio and certain property assets in Belgium and Holland) are under way with the proceeds being used to retire debt. Mike Fries , Liberty Global Chairman and CEO said : “Ziggo Group is already the most important telecommunications company in the Benelux region, with the scale to deliver the highest quality services to residential and enterprise customers and the ambition to create long-term value for shareholders. Local investors will soon have the opportunity to invest in a regional champion with strong customer propositions and a compelling outlook for free cash flow generation and dividends over time. “I’m also delighted that Vodafone will remain a 10% shareholder in the Ziggo Group. They have been an outstanding partner for nearly a decade and we will always maintain a strong relationship with Margherita and her team.” Stephen van Rooyen, VodafoneZiggo CEO and intended Ziggo Group CEO said: “ Today marks the start of Ziggo Group. For customers, nothing changes: they keep the same trusted brands they know today. Behind the scenes, though, we’re creating a stronger company with greater ability to invest, innovate and build for the future. Our ambition is simple: combine the strength of a larger group with the focus and entrepreneurial spirit of strong local businesses.” * Financial data as of December 31, 2025 and represents the combined results of the VodafoneZiggo JV and Telenet, excluding Wyre. US GAAP and IFRS are broadly similar. For more additional information please see the Liberty Global Q1 2026 investor presentation.

title: England Moves Closer to Eliminating Hepatitis C
summary: A major public health milestone is within reach as England reports strong progress in diagnosing and treating hepatitis C, while health officials continue efforts to find people who remain unaware they carry the virus. More than 100,000 people in England have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C since 2015
body_text: A major public health milestone is within reach as England reports strong progress in diagnosing and treating hepatitis C, while health officials continue efforts to find people who remain unaware they carry the virus. England is moving closer to an important public health goal: eliminating hepatitis C as a major health threat. New figures show that significant progress has been made in recent years. More than 100,000 people in England have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C since 2015, while deaths linked to the virus have fallen substantially over the past decade. The progress is particularly notable because hepatitis C can remain hidden for many years. People can live with the infection without experiencing obvious symptoms, allowing liver damage to develop silently. Health officials now want to maintain the momentum and reach people who may still be living with the virus without knowing it. What is hepatitis C? Hepatitis C is a viral infection that primarily affects the liver. It is transmitted through contact with infected blood. One of the most recognised routes of transmission is sharing needles or other equipment that may contain traces of infected blood. Historically, some people were also exposed through contaminated medical procedures and blood products. Blood donated in the UK is now screened for hepatitis C, significantly reducing the risk of transmission through the blood supply. The difficulty is that infection is not always obvious. Someone can have hepatitis C for years without feeling unwell. If the infection remains untreated, it can cause progressive liver damage. In some people, this can eventually lead to serious complications, including cirrhosis, liver failure or liver cancer. That is why finding the infection early is so important. Treatment can cure most cases One of the reasons health authorities are increasingly optimistic about eliminating hepatitis C is the effectiveness of modern treatment. Direct-acting antiviral medicines are taken as tablets, generally over a relatively short period. According to the information supplied by NHS England, treatment lasting around eight to 12 weeks can cure more than 95% of infections. This represents a major change from earlier approaches to hepatitis C treatment, which could be more difficult to tolerate and were less effective. The combination of highly effective medicines and improved testing has given public health programmes a realistic opportunity to reduce hepatitis C to very low levels. England has already reached the target of treating 80% of known cases. However, there is still work to do because some people have not yet been diagnosed. Finding people who do not know they are infected Testing is at the heart of the next stage of the campaign. According to figures for 2024, an estimated 50,200 adults were living with hepatitis C in England. Around 84.6% were thought to have been diagnosed. That means a proportion of people may still be carrying the virus without knowing it. Different approaches have therefore been introduced to make testing easier. These include blood tests offered in accident and emergency departments, testing linked to GP registration and free home-testing services. The idea is simple: if people can discover an infection without having to navigate a complicated healthcare process, more cases can be identified and treated. The NHS also provides confidential home-testing options for people who may be at increased risk. Why some people are being encouraged to test Health authorities are particularly encouraging certain groups to consider testing. Adults born in countries including Ukraine, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Albania, Lithuania, Bulgaria, Czechia and Slovakia have been highlighted because some people from these countries may have been exposed to hepatitis C through medical or dental procedures before 1991. This does not mean that everyone born in these countries has hepatitis C. Rather, it reflects historical differences in healthcare practices and infection-control standards. For people who may have been exposed decades ago, testing can provide an answer even if they have never experienced symptoms. That is important because hepatitis C is not necessarily associated with feeling ill in its early stages. A significant reduction in deaths Treatment is not only about stopping transmission. It can also prevent serious illness and save lives. The figures supplied for England show that deaths associated with hepatitis C have fallen by 36% over the past decade. The country's longer-term goal is a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality compared with 2015 levels. That target has not yet been reached, but health officials believe it could be achieved before the World Health Organization's 2030 deadline. Reaching the target will depend on continuing to diagnose people, ensuring they receive treatment and supporting those who need ongoing medical care. Lessons from the infected blood scandal The story of hepatitis C in Britain also has a painful historical dimension. Between 1970 and 1991, more than 30,000 people in the UK were infected with HIV and hepatitis C through contaminated blood products and transfusions. The resulting infected blood scandal has been described as one of the most serious treatment disasters in the history of the NHS. Thousands of people have died since being infected, and the consequences have affected families and communities for decades. The history is a reminder that infectious diseases can have consequences long after the original exposure. It also highlights why safe blood supplies, effective screening and transparent healthcare systems are so important. What happens next? England's progress is encouraging, but elimination does not mean that hepatitis C disappears overnight. There will still be people who have not been diagnosed, people who require treatment and a need to prevent new infections. Public health teams therefore face the challenge of reaching people who may not consider themselves at risk. For individuals, one of the most important steps is simply being aware that hepatitis C can exist without noticeable symptoms. A person does not necessarily need to feel unwell to benefit from testing. The availability of confidential home-testing services could make that process easier for people who are reluctant to visit a GP or discuss their medical history in person. A public health milestone within reach England's progress against hepatitis C demonstrates what can happen when effective medicines are combined with widespread testing and targeted public health programmes. More than 100,000 people have already been diagnosed and treated since 2015, and mortality has fallen considerably. The country has also met its treatment target for known infections. The remaining challenge is to find those who have not yet been diagnosed and make sure they can access treatment. If that work continues successfully, England could become one of the first countries to achieve hepatitis C elimination as a major public health problem. For a virus that can remain hidden for years but is now highly treatable, early testing could make an enormous difference. Disclaimer: This article is for general information and educational purposes only. It is not medical advice or a substitute for consultation with a qualified healthcare professional. If you think you may have been exposed to hepatitis C or have concerns about your health, speak with an appropriate healthcare provider or use an official NHS testing service. Always rely on current guidance from the NHS and other recognised public health authorities for medical decisions.

title: The Stoic Letters, 3rd August
summary: In Praise of the Pen: A letter on what handwriting does to the mind
body_text: Dear Stoics, All the good old stuff is coming back lately: first vinyl, then retro film cameras. Now the paper notebook is having its moment, and stationery shops all over the world are busy again. It would be easy to dismiss this as one more vintage trend, but the neuroscience suggests it’s much more than that. At the Norwegian University of Science and Technology, researchers fitted university students with a 256-electrode EEG net, and asked them to write words, sometimes by hand, sometimes on a keyboard, while their brain activity was recorded. The difference was striking: handwriting lit up widespread, interconnected activity across brain regions, in frequency bands associated with memory formation and the encoding of new information. Typing produced nothing even comparable. The researchers’ explanation was that forming each letter is an act that engages both the mind and the whole body. The hand and eye movements differ with every character, while a keystroke is the same tiny, repeatable motion, whatever you’re typing. This nicely complements an older classroom finding: students who take notes grasp concepts better than laptop or phone note-takers, precisely because they write more slowly. Hand-writers can’t keep up with the speed of spoken words, so they must digest, compress, and choose wisely what to note. The slowness is exactly where the thinking happens. (Scientists still debate how directly brain patterns translate into better learning, and some findings await replication. But the direction of the evidence and of lived experience points the same way: the hand and the mind are great coworkers.) Beyond the science, there is the sensory case, which is just as satisfying. Ink has friction, and paper has a feel to it. A handwritten sentence cannot be deleted, only crossed out, which changes how carefully we choose it. It also leaves its mark on how our notes look. A filled notebook is also an object: years from now, you can hold it again and remember how you felt while pouring your heart onto the page. You may reasonably raise an eyebrow, as this praise of paper arrives from an app, but we’re okay with that. Our conviction has always been that the journaling that actually happens beats the ideal journaling. A journal with a screen is far more handy when you need to write something on a bus or while travelling. But a practice can have two instruments: the app for the daily notes, and the pen for the occasional slower, deliberate reflection. By no means should they be considered rivals. So here is this week’s invitation: write one entry by hand. Any paper will do: a dedicated notebook or the back of an envelope. Pick something that’s been on your mind and notice how differently sentences form when they cannot be deleted. If what surfaces is worth keeping, copy its essence into your journal in Stoic , or photograph the page and keep the original somewhere safe, the way one keeps letters. Yours truly, The Stoic App Team P.S. Here’s more about the wonders of handwriting: Handwriting activates broader brain networks than typing, study shows Does writing by hand still matter in a digital world? According to a new study in Frontiers in Psychology, the answer is yes. PsyPost - Psychology News • Eric W. Dolan Frontiers | Handwriting but not typewriting leads to widespread brain connectivity: a high-density EEG study with implications for the classroom As traditional handwriting is progressively being replaced by digital devices, it is essential to investigate the implications for the human brain. Brain ele... Frontiers Writing by Hand is Good for your Brain - Here's how to do it Because I am known to write using a fountain pen on paper, a number of people have pointed me to this post and its underlying research. I won’t rehash what is said in those sources, but the gist of it is that when you write things down by hand you’re recruiting more of your brain, which is a good thing. Neal Stephenson A letter always feels to me like immortality. Emily Dickinson The word alone makes most of us flinch, as we picture raised voices, slammed doors, things that can’t be later unsaid. But this week’s theme, On Confrontations , is about a gentler discovery: that facing something head-on is usually far more okay than the weeks of walking around it. We all have our carefully avoided objects. For some time, avoidance feels like peace, but it’s really just conflict charging us every day. So this week, we’ll practise looking directly at things with no dramatic arguments ahead. The safest place to hold your first confrontation is a page only you can read, so open your journal and start whenever you feel like.
